- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- After a model forecast spike (e.g., >70.5), true price often reverses or corrects within 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward bias to subsequent forecasts if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and model shows rising trend, model overestimates recovery; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in the 7–14 day horizon when sentiment is positive; apply +2–4% bias to forecast for days 7–14 if sentiment >0.6.
- If model forecast is flat or slightly rising while sentiment is negative, true price often drops sharply; add 1–3% downward adjustment to next 3–5 days.
- Model tends to lag true price by 2–4 days in upward moves; if sentiment is positive, forecast should be adjusted up by 1–2% for the next 2–3 days to catch momentum.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overfits recent noise; apply smoothing filter or reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% for next 5 days.
